label: a8-02-thm-tarski-square
tail:
ALLEGATION_VERDICT: NOT_REAL
ALLEGATION_LOCATION: items/thm-tarski-square.md lines 68, 82, 84, and 86
ALLEGATION_ITEM_QUOTE: “therefore (2) applies to $B$ and we may fix a bijection”; “[L7] There is no injection ...; a set is finite when it is equinumerous with a natural number”
ALLEGATION_TARGET_QUOTE: items/def-injection-surjection-bijection.md line 46: “$f$ is bijective if it is both injective and surjective.” items/thm-cardinal-arithmetic-agrees-with-finite-counting.md lines 48–51: “If $A$ is finite ([[def-countable]]) then $A$ is well-orderable”
ALLEGATION_REASONING: Step 3.1 proves that B is infinite and then invokes statement (2), which by definition supplies a bijection from the square of B onto B. The first case of step 4.1 really does produce an injection into A itself, exactly contradicting Hartogs. The judge also misread L7: it contains both the pigeonhole claim and the separate definition of finiteness. A finite set is well-orderable by transporting the standard well-order of its equinumerous von Neumann natural; the declared finite-counting dependency states this explicitly.

OTHER_FINDINGS: NONE
